### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **187** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f0ccd789898c8d8d7315652a2bbce2f4973d803e` — the merge of head `8a85482aea33f2377b89ffa53dd360212c78480e` into base `9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f0ccd789898c8d8d7315652a2bbce2f4973d803e && git checkout f0ccd789898c8d8d7315652a2bbce2f4973d803e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8 8a85482aea33f2377b89ffa53dd360212c78480e && git checkout -B drift-repro 9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8 && git merge --no-ff 8a85482aea33f2377b89ffa53dd360212c78480e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9c283a11bfc189e2a96e84b3f8b66cbdbd994cb8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6303c52011b85208bd7e56d9f6a1a539eb0bd81e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-object-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-action-layout.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts, ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts, ui/packages/types/src/index.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewPageHeader.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/layout/record-header-bar-context.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/designModeHeaderPins.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/designModeHeaderPinsSave.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/DesignModeHeaderPins.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/DesignModeHeaderPinsPanel.tsx

Net diff judged against merge-base `4ef1ea9779` (75 files, +3445 / -72). Read outside the diff, not reviewed: `docs/adr/0085` §1-§2 and `docs/adr/0146` D2 / D10 on main, `packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-arrangement.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (the level rule), weekly card #36086.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectSchema` gains optional `actionLayout: { list?, record? }`, each arm a strict `{ pinned (required, at most 3), more? }`. The object was strict before, so the key was refused and is now accepted: a widening. Right.
- `ObjectExtensionSchema` gains the same leaf (one shared `OBJECT_ACTION_LAYOUT_SCHEMA`). Also a widening by parse. Right as a parse fact; wrong as a contract, see M1: the key is admitted for every extension package, and no door or fold rule narrows the writer.
- Shape refusals read in the source: more than 3 pinned, a name twice in one part, a name in both parts, a malformed name, a `$` built-in the scope lacks, an unknown key in an arm or in the leaf. `pinned: []` and `more: []` are accepted. The same name in both arms is accepted, which is right (an action may be placed in both scopes). The entry pattern is `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema`'s (two characters at least), read in `identifiers.zod.ts`. Right.
- New `@objectstack/spec/data` exports: `OBJECT_ACTION_LAYOUT_PINNED_LIMIT`, `OBJECT_ACTION_LAYOUT_SCOPES`, `OBJECT_ACTION_LAYOUT_BUILTINS`, types `ObjectActionLayoutScope`, `ObjectActionLayout`, `ObjectActionLayoutArm`. The leaf schema itself stays unexported, as the icon leaf does. Right.
- Dropped-refinements baseline GROWS: `droppedRefinementSites` 1151 to 1171, 20 new sites, `actionLayout.list` and `actionLayout.record` at each of the ten published schemas that embed an object or an object extension. The refinement dropped is the arm's uniqueness `superRefine`; the `max 3` and the entry pattern do project. So a JSON-Schema-only validator accepts a repeated name that every zod door refuses. The source says so ("the one rule JSON Schema is not given here"), the count of schemas with drops stays 274, and the reader counts a repeated name once. Right, a declared contract fact.
- `@objectstack/lint`: one new gating rule (`object-action-layout-unknown`, `object-action-layout-not-placed`, error, CLI only), the 77th. It can refuse only a stack that writes the new key, so nothing accepted before is refused now. Right.
- `@objectstack/objectql`: `OBJECT_FOLD_SCALAR_KEYS` gains `actionLayout`; the extension's value folds arm by arm, last extender by priority. The packaged base is untouched (read in the fold and its test). The yield is computed per key, not per arm: S2.
- `@objectstack/metadata-core`: `OBJECT_REFERENCE_POSITIONS.actionLayout: keep`. Right: the key holds action names, no field names.
- `@object-ui/types`: new exports `arrangedHeaderActions`, `readActionLayoutArm`, `ActionLayoutArm`. `@object-ui/components`: `RecordHeaderState` gains an optional `actionLayout`. Additive.
- Check-runs on this head: every completed run is success or skipped (Build Core, Test Core 1-8 and 10 of 10, Test UI 1-16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset first run, PR-body guards, the lint and type-check families). Two were still `in_progress` when read: Test Core (9/10), and a second Check Changeset run started 05:16Z by a PR-body edit. The PR is a draft.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). True: every refusal the diff adds sits inside the new key, and no previously accepted document is refused.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is true (a new authorable key on two schemas). The changeset gives `minor` to spec, objectql, lint and `@object-ui/types`, and `patch` to metadata-core, platform-objects, `@object-ui/components`, app-shell and i18n. The gate's rule, read in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, is "at least one moved package minor or above"; the first Check Changeset run on this head is green. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` moves only a test file and needs no entry. The level holds.

The changeset body describes the extension fold as "the last extender by priority wins", which is what the code does; it changes with the fix of M1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- SQL push-down: none. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Deviation "ADR notes go to carrier #36086, not written to docs/adr": not accepted as it stands for the ADR-0085 row, see S1, and row 2 depends on M1. Seat ruling 7080672229 said "Owed in the same PR"; the claim 7088319611 moved them out. The carrier pattern has precedent for an ADR-0146 D10 note (#36517's row on the same card), so the route alone is no finding.
- Deviation "no new door-level code and status test": accepted. The shape refusals are pinned in `packages/spec`; the server door refuses shape only.
- Deviation "app-shell tests narrowed locally": answered by CI, Test UI 1-16 green on this head.
- Deviation "live run pinned Import, record scope not run live": lane's ACCEPT; not a contract matter.
- Deviations on the four-line summary, the `registry-top-level.ts` placement of the fold (facade ceiling kept) and the four transcript counts: accepted.
- Open question 1 (route the contract review at this head): answered by this record.
- Open question 2 (panel wording with no list arm): the panel wording may stay, but the same gap is in the spec's own sentences, see S4.
- Assumptions 1-6, 8, 10: consistent with rulings 7077698148 and 7080672229 and with the code read. Assumption 2 (the record arm also orders the phone bar) departs from the card's "不改手机底部的按钮条" and is covered by ruling 7080672229. Assumption 7 (`.custom` replaces an arm whole): the code grants it to every extension, M1. Assumption 9 (save refusals): the server refuses shape only; the reference refusals are the CLI's and the design mode's own, N1. Assumption 11: S4.
- Carrier row 2 on #36086 (comment 7091884833) says unknown or not-allowed action ids are "refused at save with a named reason (422 `INVALID_METADATA`)". The PR's own acceptance notes and the code say the server refuses a malformed arrangement only. The row is wrong as written and must not be ticked in that wording.

### ④ Design judgment

**(A) ADR-0085 §2.** Judged on the ADR's text on main.

Test 1 (business intent not inferable). "Which actions matter most here, in order" is the same kind of intent `highlightFields` and the 2026-10-28 `relatedLists` note were admitted on. It is weaker here: each action already carries `order`, a `record_header` or `record_more` placement, `component: 'action:menu'` and `variant`, and the keyless default is derived from exactly those. What the key adds is a second, per-scope statement of a priority the schema already carries, plus a place where a party that does not own the actions can restate it. That is a customization-layer need (ADR-0146), not a fact the machine cannot know.

Test 2 (bound across surfaces, no page name). The `record` arm passes on today's tree: one arm is read by the record page header, the side preview and the phone bar (`RecordDetailView.tsx`, `containers.tsx`). The `list` arm does not pass on today's tree: its only reader is the list page toolbar (`objectViewPageHeader.tsx`), its built-ins are "the list page's", the object form labels it "The list page toolbar", and the leaf's own alias map expects authors to write `listPage` and `recordPage`. Its second surface is promised by #36494 and #36496, not present. The card's own item 6 asks for storage "按页面类型".

"Merely re-arranging correct information": yes, literally. The key orders actions and moves them between buttons and More; it adds and removes nothing. §2 rejects that class at this layer, and the 2026-11-20 note calls `relatedLists` "the one place" the sentence yields and says "the guard keeps its force for every other key".

Precedent. Partly analogous (an ordered list of what matters on the object). Not analogous in the two ways that counted: related lists had no order-carrying key of their own, and that admission was recorded as a ruled exception quoting the maintainer, inside the PR that landed the key (#35923 touched the ADR file; so did #36236 for `place`). Here the note is one unticked carrier line, and it words the admission as a test pass ("each arm binds every surface of its scope and names no page"), which the `list` arm does not support.

So: the key does not enter by the two tests alone. It enters only as a second ruled exception. The maintainer did decide the substance (「放在对象上,分列表和记录」 and the 14:50Z ruling, as relayed in 7080672229 and 7087101113), so the placement itself is not overturned here. What is missing is the record: the ADR text on main is false the moment this merges, and `object-action-layout.ts` cites §2 as if it supported the key.

S1 (should-fix) — ADR-0085 §2 is contradicted, not satisfied, and the hits file cites it as support ("An arm is a scope, not a page (ADR-0085 §2 keeps per-page keys off the object)"). Resolution: a `needs-user-decision` on card #36366 asking the maintainer to confirm `actionLayout` as a ruled exception to §2's re-arrange sentence, with the `list` arm's single surface stated; the dated note then quotes those words, amends "the one place", and lands in the weekly ADR PR no later than this PR merges (carrier row 1 reworded from "admitted as a cross-surface role" to a ruled exception). The jsdoc sentence in `object-action-layout.ts` is reworded to cite the note, not the test. Renaming the arms or moving the key to the assigned-page layer are the alternatives if the maintainer declines.

**(B) ADR-0146 D10.** D10's 2026-11-22 note: an extension "places only what it brings ... the base's arrangement stays the base's"; the maintainer's words in `field-customization.ts`: 「继承软件包 ... 只能申明插入位置，原始软件包、环境管理员 应该可以申明完整的配置」; D2: the overrider "is fixed by role, never by publish order". Ruling 7080672229 admits one writer ("`.custom` replaces one arm whole"), and carrier row 2 calls it "the one thing the paired `.custom` arranges on the base's own items".

The code does not implement that. `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS` is still `['fieldGroups', 'relatedLists']`; `judgeExtensionArrangement` and the CLI door read that list, so no door refuses `actionLayout` in a package that is not a `.custom` package; `foldExtensionActionLayout` runs for every extender in priority order with no role test. The PR's own test pins the result: a partner package at priority 250 beats the pair at 150 ("two extenders resolve by priority"). At the default priority (200 for both, and the design mode's Save writes none) the winner is whichever registered last. `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx` lists the key as open to any extension, beside the row that reserves `fieldGroups` and `relatedLists` to the pair.

M1 (must-fix) — `ObjectExtensionSchema.actionLayout` is writable by any extension package and is resolved by priority, so (1) a package that is not the pair replaces an arm whole and re-arranges the base's own actions, which D10's note forbids for every other arrangement and no ruling admits, and (2) the administrator's saved arrangement in the pair can lose to an installed partner package, silently, which breaks the card's "保存后所有成员看到的页头都跟着变". It must be settled before the key is first published, because refusing a writer later is a narrowing. Either: put `actionLayout` under the pair's writer rule (refused outside a `.custom` package at save, publish, install, `os validate` and `os build` by the one judge; applied by role in the fold, the object's pair only, after the other extenders; the key's own describe carrying the writer sentence; the priority test rewritten); or obtain a maintainer ruling on the card that any extender may re-arrange the base's actions, and then say how the pair still wins. The docs row, the changeset sentence and carrier row 2 follow the choice.

S2 (should-fix) — the fold is per arm but the yield is per key. `tenantAuthoredScalars` adds `actionLayout` when the base's value differs from the packaged owner's in either arm, and `foldExtensionActionLayout` then skips the extension's whole value. A tenant that arranged only `list` on the base makes an extension's `record` arm disappear, though no tenant value exists for that scope. The schema jsdoc and the docs say "applied arm by arm" and "a value the tenant authored on the base stays"; neither says the other arm is dropped. Yield per arm, or state the key-level yield in the describe and the docs.

S3 (should-fix) — the design mode's Save writes arms the administrator did not change. `DesignModeHeaderPinsPanel` stages `{ ...current, [page]: ... }` where `current` starts as the served (folded) `actionLayout`, and `saveObjectPins` writes `actionLayoutValue(pins)`, both arms. Changing the record scope on an installed object therefore copies the base's (or another extender's) `list` arm into the pair's `object_extension`, where it masks every later change the vendor makes to that arm; on a writable package it copies an extender's arm into the object itself. The module's own contract sentence is "Each arm the administrator changed is written whole". Write only the arms that differ from what the target document already holds.

S4 (should-fix) — the list scope's built-ins do not follow the sentences the spec publishes. `more` is described as "the order of the scope's 「More」 menu", and the schema accepts `$import` and `$export` there, but `PinnedListHeaderActions` leaves a built-in named in `more` (or named nowhere) in the page's own Import / Export entry, outside the toolbar's overflow: the value is accepted and orders nothing. `pinned: []` is described as "draws none", yet the list bar still draws the `Import ▾` menu at its end. The docs example teaches `list: { ..., more: ['$import'] }`. Either refuse a built-in in `list.more`, or state in the describe, the form help and the docs that a built-in is only ever pinned and otherwise keeps its own entry, and drop it from the example.

Per file otherwise:

- `object-action-layout.ts`: the shape matches rulings 7080672229 and the 14:50Z words (two arms, `pinned` at most 3 and required, `more` optional). Refusal messages name the reason and the fix. Apart from S1 and S4 the jsdoc agrees with the readers: unnamed actions follow at the end of More in their own order (`rest` keeps authored `order`, named ones take a far-negative rank); a hidden pinned action leaves its slot empty (unpinned record actions become `record_more` only and unpinned list actions `action:menu`, so none is promoted).
- `object.zod.ts`: the two key placements and the guidance text are right; the extension key carries only the shared describe, so the published reference for the extension says nothing of the fold or the writer (covered by M1).
- `object.form.ts`: one JSON row per arm; the help text states honestly that only `os validate` refuses an unknown or unplaced name and that such a name draws nothing.
- `index.ts`: exports as listed in ①.
- `validate-object-action-layout.ts`: `ARM_LOCATIONS` equals the readers' (`list_toolbar`; `record_header` or `record_more`, the same pair `placedHeaderActions` filters on). An extension of an object the stack does not define is not judged, which means the main write path (the pair's extension of an installed object) is never judged by the CLI.
- `ui-action.ts`, `RecordDetailView.tsx`, `containers.tsx`, `objectViewPageHeader.tsx`: one reader, applied after `placedHeaderActions` (record) or to the toolbar's own action list (list). Security holds: the reader only re-orders and re-places action objects it is handed, spreads each action whole so `visible` and permission predicates travel with it, and a name that matches nothing draws nothing; pinning cannot surface an action the header would not already be handed. An authored `page:header` with its own `actions` keeps its list. The approval levers are unchanged.

N1 (nit) — reference checks (unknown name, wrong scope) exist only in the CLI rule and in the design mode's client-side Save; a direct `PUT` or the Studio form's JSON row stores any well-formed name, and the pair's extension is outside the CLI rule. The effect is benign (draws nothing; the panel lists the name as left out), and a later package version can produce the same state legitimately. Ruling 7077698148's "refused at save with a named reason" is met by the design mode's Save only; carrier row 2 must stop claiming the 422.

N2 (nit) — `foldExtensionActionLayout` spreads `extension.actionLayout` without a record test. An unparsed manifest body with a non-record value, or `{}`, leaves a junk or empty `actionLayout` on the served object. The UI reader tolerates both.

N3 (nit) — an arm cannot order More without also fixing the buttons (`pinned` is required), so "keep the default buttons, re-order More" is not expressible. It follows the ruled format; noted for #36494.

## 席位核对
ACCEPT — L1 for card #36366 at head `6303c52011b85208bd7e56d9f6a1a539eb0bd81e` (2026-11-23T05:25Z), read by the card thread (seat repo:objectstack#2, area s2-B). Contract-tier L2 owed on the same head (claim 7092292631 by l2-review#4); landing is the seat's (3517 changed lines > 3000 ⇒ human-merge path, the seat hands off to the approver).

- **Shape:** open draft to `main`; first line `Fixes #36366` (the whole card: list and record arms, panel, save, headers, preview, phone bar); no closing keyword next to any other card; no `content/docs/releases/` path. Declarations `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Skills-docs: follow-up #36630` (filed by the seat), in the body and the changeset.
- **Premise:** re-measured at the claim (7088319611): no `actionLayout` / `pinnedActions` on main; the release's condition (#36363 merged) holds. The branch resumes seat 7's parked `claude/project-thread-bm91dz@b5392415`; its 8 commits are all on this branch (checked by subject), rebased onto main.
- **Gates (check-runs at this head):** 63 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check success; `mergeable_state` clean. Local: `dispatch-gates --ran` 130 derived / 130 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED at 564840dc1b, and the families the main merge touched re-run at this head (`/mnt/project-files/objectstack-seat2/36366-gates-ran.txt`). One ablation: `arrangedHeaderActions`' `moreAt` blanked ⇒ the 3 more-order tests red, controls green, restored blob identical.
- **Spot reads:**
  - `packages/spec/src/data/object-action-layout.ts`: closed arms (`strictObject`, aliases named), `pinned` required and capped at 3 with a reason naming where the rest go, the entry regex (snake_case or the scope's `$` built-ins) carried into JSON Schema, uniqueness across both parts by `superRefine`; the same leaf on `ObjectSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema`, and the extension guidance sentence lists `actionLayout` among the carried keys.
  - `packages/objectql/src/registry-top-level.ts`: `actionLayout` joins the fold scalars; an extension arm replaces the running arm whole, arm by arm; the D9.2a yield asks the structural `foldScalarOverridesPackagedBase` (no owner ⇒ false, an empty value ⇒ false, exact equality). Tests cover extension-only, arm replaced whole, priority order, tenant-authored stays, and a re-order-only overlay counted as authored.
  - `ui/packages/types/src/ui-action.ts` `arrangedHeaderActions`: no arm ⇒ the input unchanged; pinned lead in pin order, named `more` next, the rest in default order; unknown or hidden names skipped with no substitution.
  - `designModeHeaderPinsSave.ts`: refuses an unknown or not-placed name before any write; writes the object's own package when writable, else an `object_extension` in the ensured pair; first-write pin (`ifNoneMatch: '*'`) so a pending draft is refused; a refused publish discards the draft.
  - Changeset and docs read sentence by sentence: `.changeset/36366-object-action-layout.md`, `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` (new section), `data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`, `references/system/migration.mdx`, `references/api/metadata.mdx`, the generated `references/data/object.mdx` row, and the four CLI transcripts (76 → 77 rules).
